{{No footnotes|date=August 2022}}
'''Goodman's conjecture on the coefficients of [[multivalent function|multivalent function]]s''' was proposed in [[complex analysis]] in 1948 by [[Adolph Winkler Goodman]], an American mathematician.

== Formulation ==
Let <math>f(z)= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}{b_n z^n}</math> be a <math>p</math>-valent function. The conjecture claims the following coefficients hold:
<math display="block">|b_n| \le \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k(n+p)!}{(p-k)!(p+k)!(n-p-1)!(n^2-k^2)}|b_k|</math>

== Partial results ==
It's known that when <math>p=2,3</math>, the conjecture is true for functions of the form <math>P \circ \phi</math> where <math>P</math> is a [[polynomial]] and <math>\phi</math> is [[univalent function|univalent]].
